paragraphs.sourceText: Among the kinds of social gestures most significant for second-language teachers are those which are 26 in form but different in meaning in the two cultures. For example, a Colombian who wants someone to 27 him often signals with a hand movement in which all the fingers of one hand, cupped, point downward as they move rapidly 28 . Speakers of English have a similar gesture though the hand may not be cupped and the fingers may be held more loosely, but for them the gesture means goodbye or go away, quite the 29 of the Colombian gesture. Again, in Colombia, a speaker of English would have to know that when he 30 height he must choose between different gestures depending on whether he is 31 a human being or an animal. If he keeps the palm of the hand 32 the floor, as he would in his own culture when making known the height of a child, for example, he will very likely be greeted by laughter; in Colombia this gesture is 33 for the description of animals. In order to describe human beings he should keep the palm of his hand 34 to the floor. Substitutions of one gesture for the other often create not only humorous but also 35 moments. In both of the examples above, speakers from two different cultures have the same gesture, physically, but its meaning differs sharply.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于第二语言教师来说最重要的社交手势是那些在两种文化中形式相同但含义不同的手势。例如，哥伦比亚人希望有人接近他时，通常会通过手势来发出信号，其中一只手的所有手指呈杯状，向下快速移动。说英语的人也有类似的手势，尽管手可能不会呈杯状，手指可能会握得更松，但对他们来说，这个手势意味着再见或走开，与哥伦比亚手势完全相反。同样，在哥伦比亚，说英语的人必须知道，当他表示身高时，他必须根据他指的是人类还是动物在不同的手势之间进行选择。例如，如果他将手掌与地板保持平行，就像在他自己的文化中那样，当他知道孩子的身高时，他很可能会受到笑声的欢迎。在哥伦比亚，这个手势是为描述动物而保留的。为了描述人类，他应该保持手掌与地板成直角。用一种姿势代替另一种姿势常常不仅会产生幽默，还会产生尴尬的时刻。在上面的两个例子中，来自两种不同文化的说话者在肢体上有相同的手势，但其含义却截然不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many Brazilians cannot read. In 2000, a quarter of those aged 15 and older were functionally illiterate (文盲）.Many 36 do not want to. Only one literate adult in three reads books. The 37 Brazilian reads 1. 8 non-academic books a year, less than half the figure in Europe and the United States. In a recent survey of reading habits, Brazilians came 27th out of 30 countries. Argentines, their neighbors, 38 18th.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多巴西人不识字。 2000年，15岁及以上的人中有四分之一是功能性文盲（文盲）。许多人只是不想这样做。只有三分之一的成年人读书。巴西人平均每年阅读1. 8本非学术书籍，不到欧洲和美国这一数字的一半。在最近的一项阅读习惯调查中，巴西人在30个国家中排名第27位。他们的邻国阿根廷排名第18位。

paragraphs.sourceText: The government and businesses are all struggling in different ways to change this. On March 13 the government 39 a National Plan for Books and Reading. This seeks to boost reading, by founding libraries and financing publishers among other things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 政府和企业都在以不同的方式努力改变这一现状。 3月13日，政府启动了国家图书和阅读计划。该计划旨在通过建立图书馆和资助出版商等方式促进阅读。

paragraphs.sourceText: One discouragement to reading is that books are 40 . Most books have small print-runs, pushing up their price.
paragraphs.translationZh: 读书的一大障碍是书籍价格昂贵。大多数书籍的印数很少，从而推高了它们的价格。

paragraphs.sourceText: But Brazilians5 indifference to books has deeper roots. Centuries of slavery meant the country’s leaders long 41 education. Primary schooling became universal only in the 1990s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但巴西人对书籍的冷漠有着更深的根源。几个世纪的奴隶制意味着该国领导人长期忽视教育。小学教育直到 20 世纪 90 年代才普及。

paragraphs.sourceText: All this means Brazil’s book market has the biggest growth 42 in the western world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一切都意味着巴西的图书市场拥有西方世界最大的增长潜力。

paragraphs.sourceText: But reading is a difficult habit to form. Brazilians bought fewer books in 2004, 89 million, including textbooks 43 by the government, than they did in 1991. Last year the director of Brazil’s national library 44 . He complained that he had half the librarians he needed and termites (白蚁）had eaten much of the 45 . That ought to be a cause for national shame.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但阅读是一个很难养成的习惯。 2004 年，巴西人购买的图书比 1991 年减少了 8900 万册，其中包括政府分发的教科书。去年，巴西国家图书馆馆长辞职了。他抱怨说，他所需要的图书管理员只有一半，而白蚁（白蚁）已经吃掉了大部分藏书。这应该成为全国耻辱的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions ：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. The Touch-Screen Generation
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答卷 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。 触摸屏一代

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On a chilly day last spring, a few dozen developers of children’s apps(应用程序）for phones and tablets(平板电脑) gathered at an old beach resort in Monterey, California, to show off their games. The gathering was organized by Warren Buckleitner, a longtime reviewer of interactive children’s media. Buckleitner spent the breaks testing whether his own remote-control helicopter could reach the hairs second story, while various children who had come with their parents looked up in awe(敬畏）and delight. But mostly they looked down, at the iPads and other tablets displayed around the hall like so many open boxes of candy. I walked around and talked with developers, and several quoted a famous saying of Maria Montessori’s, “ The hands are the instruments of man’s intelligence.’’
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 去年春天的一个寒冷的日子，几十个手机和平板电脑儿童应用程序的开发者聚集在加利福尼亚州蒙特雷的一个古老的海滩度假村，展示他们的游戏。这次聚会是由互动儿童媒体的长期评论家沃伦·巴克莱特纳 (Warren Buckleitner) 组织的。巴克莱特纳在休息时间测试他自己的遥控直升机是否可以到达头发的第二层，而与父母一起来的各个孩子都带着敬畏和喜悦抬头看着。他们低头看着大厅里展示的 iPad 和其他平板电脑，就像许多打开的糖果盒一样。我四处走动并与开发人员交谈，其中一些人引用了玛丽亚·蒙特梭利的一句名言：“手是人类智力的工具。”

paragraphs.sourceText: B) What, really, would Maria Montessori have made of this scene? The 30 or so children here were not down at the shore poking (戳) their fingers in the sand or running them along stones or picking seashells. Instead they were all inside, alone or in groups of two or three, their faces a few inches from a screen, their hands doing things Montessori surely did not imagine.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 玛丽亚·蒙台梭利真的会如何看待这个场景？这里大约有 30 个孩子，他们并没有在岸边把手指戳进沙子里，也没有沿着石头奔跑，也没有捡贝壳。相反，他们都在里面，单独或两三人一组，他们的脸距离屏幕几英寸，他们的手做着蒙台梭利肯定无法想象的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) In 2011, the American Academy of Pediatrics updated its policy on very young children and media. In 1999, the group had discouraged television viewing for children younger than 2, citing research on brain development that showed this age groups critical need for “direct interactions with parents and other significant care givers.” The updated report began by acknowledging that things had changed significantly since then. In 2006, 90% of parents said that their children younger than 2 consumed some form of electronic media. Nevertheless, the group took largely the same approach it did in 1999, uniformly discouraging passive media use, on any type of screen, for these kids. (For older children, the academy noted, “high-quality programs” could have “educational benefits.” ）The 2011 report mentioned “smart cell phone” and “new screen” technologies, but did not address interactive apps. Nor did it bring up the possibility that has likely occurred to those 90% of American parents that some good might come from those little swiping（在电子产品上刷）fingers.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 2011 年，美国儿科学会更新了其关于幼儿和媒体的政策。 1999年，该组织不鼓励两岁以下儿童看电视，理由是大脑发育研究表明这个年龄段的孩子迫切需要“与父母和其他重要的照顾者直接互动”。更新后的报告首先承认自那时以来情况发生了重大变化。 2006年，90%的父母表示他们两岁以下的孩子消费某种形式的电子媒体。尽管如此，该组织采取的做法与 1999 年基本相同，一致不鼓励这些孩子在任何类型的屏幕上使用被动媒体。 （该学院指出，对于年龄较大的孩子来说，“高质量的节目”可能具有“教育效益”。）2011 年的报告提到了“智能手机”和“新屏幕”技术，但没有提及交互式应用程序。它也没有提到 90% 的美国父母可能会想到的可能性，即那些小小的手指可能会带来一些好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) I had come to the developers, conference partly because I hoped that this particular set of parents, enthusiastic as they were about interactive media, might help me out of this problem, that they might offer some guiding principle for American parents who are clearly never going to meet the academy’s ideals, and at some level do not want to. Perhaps this group would be able to express clearly some benefits of the new technology that the more cautious doctors weren’t ready to address.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）我来参加开发者会议，部分原因是我希望这群对互动媒体充满热情的特殊家长可以帮助我解决这个问题，他们可以为美国家长提供一些指导原则，他们显然永远不会实现学院的理想，并且在某种程度上也不想实现。也许这个小组能够清楚地表达新技术的一些好处，而更为谨慎的医生还没有准备好解决这些好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) I fell into conversation with a woman who had helped develop Montessori Letter Sounds, an app that teaches preschoolers the Montessori methods of spelling. She was a former Montessori teacher and a mother of four. I myself have three children who are all fans of the touch screen. What games did her kids like to play, I asked, hoping for suggestions I could take home. “ They don’t play all that much. ” Really? Why not? “Because I don’t allow it. We have a rule of no screen time during the week, unless it’s clearly educational. ’’ No screen time? None at all? That seems at the outer edge of restrictive, even by the standards of overcontrolling parents. “On the weekends, they can play. I give them a limit of half an hour and then stop. Enough.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 我与一位帮助开发 Montessori Letter Sounds 的女士进行了交谈，这是一款教学龄前儿童蒙特梭利拼写方法的应用程序。她曾是一名蒙特梭利老师，也是四个孩子的母亲。我自己有三个孩子，他们都是触摸屏的粉丝。我问她的孩子喜欢玩什么游戏，希望我能把建议带回家。 “他们玩得不多。”真的吗？为什么不呢？ “因为我不允许。我们有一条规定，一周内不准看屏幕，除非它明显有教育意义。”“没有屏幕时间？根本没有？即使按照过度控制的父母的标准，这似乎也处于限制的边缘。“周末，他们可以玩。我给他们半小时的限制，然后就停下来。足够的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Her answer so surprised me that I decided to ask some of the other developers who were also parents what their domestic ground rules for screen time were. One said only on airplanes and long car rides. Another said Wednesdays. and weekends, for half an hour. The most permissive said half an hour a day, which was about my rule at home. At one point I sat with one of the biggest developers of e-book apps for kids, and his family. The small kid was starting to fuss in her high chair, so the mom stuck an iPad in front of her and played a short movie so everyone else could enjoy their lunch. When she saw me watching, she gave me the universal tense look of mothers who feel they are being judged. “ At home,” she assured me, “ I only let her watch movies in Spanish. ’”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 她的回答让我大吃一惊，因此我决定询问其他一些同样为人父母的开发者，他们国内对于屏幕时间的基本规则是什么。有人说只在飞机和长途汽车旅行时。另一个说周三。周末，半小时。最宽松的说每天半小时，这就是我在家的规定。有一次，我与最大的儿童电子书应用程序开发商之一及其家人坐在一起。小孩子开始在她的高脚椅上闹腾，所以妈妈在她面前放了一台 iPad，播放了一段短片，这样其他人就可以享受午餐了。当她看到我在观看时，她向我投来了一种普遍的紧张表情，就像那些感到自己受到评判的母亲一样。 “在家里，”她向我保证，“我只让她看西班牙语电影。 ’”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) By their reactions, these parents made me understand the problem of our age: as technology becomes almost everywhere in our lives, American parents are becoming more, not less, distrustful of what it might be doing to their children. Technological ability has not, for parents, translated into comfort and ease. On the one hand, parents want their children to swim expertly in the digital stream that they will have to navigate (航行) all their lives; on the other hand, they fear that too much digital media, too early, will sink them. Parents end up treating tablets as precision surgical (外科的）instruments, devices that might perform miracles for their child’s IQ and help him win some great robotics competition——but only if they are used just so. Otherwise, their child could end up one of those sad, pale creatures who can^ make eye contact and has a girlfriend who lives only in the virtual world.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 通过他们的反应，这些父母让我理解了我们这个时代的问题：随着技术在我们生活中几乎无处不在，美国父母越来越不信任它可能对他们的孩子造成的影响。对于父母来说，技术能力并没有转化为舒适和轻松。一方面，父母希望他们的孩子能够熟练地在数字流中游泳，而他们一生都必须在数字流中航行；另一方面，他们担心太多、太早的数字媒体会让他们沉沦。父母最终将平板电脑视为精密外科仪器，这些设备可能会为孩子的智商创造奇迹，并帮助他赢得一些伟大的机器人比赛——但前提是它们必须如此使用。否则，他们的孩子最终可能会成为那些悲伤、苍白的生物，无法进行眼神交流，并且有一个只生活在虚拟世界中的女朋友。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Norman Rockwell, a 20th-century artist, never painted Boy Swiping Finger on Screen, and our own vision of a perfect childhood has never been adjusted to accommodate that now-common scene. Add to that our modem fear that every parenting decision may have lasting consequences—that every minute of enrichment lost or mindless entertainment indulged（放纵的）will add up to some permanent handicap (障碍)in the future—and you have deep guilt and confusion. To date, no body of research has proved that the iPad will make your preschooler smarter or teach her to speak Chinese, or alternatively that it will rust her nervous system—the device has been out for only three years, not much more than the time it takes some academics to find funding and gather research subjects. So what is a parent to do?
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 20 世纪的艺术家诺曼·洛克威尔 (Norman Rockwell) 从未在屏幕上画过《男孩在屏幕上滑动手指》，而我们对完美童年的憧憬也从未被调整以适应现在常见的场景。除此之外，我们现代人还担心，每一个养育子女的决定都可能产生持久的后果——失去的每一分钟充实感或沉迷于无意识的娱乐都会在未来造成某种永久性的障碍——你会感到深深的内疚和困惑。迄今为止，还没有任何研究证明 iPad 会让你的学龄前儿童变得更聪明，或者教她说中文，或者会腐蚀他们的神经系统——该设备问世仅三年，比一些学者寻找资金和收集研究课题所需的时间长不了多少。那么家长该怎么办呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. The author attended the conference, hoping to find some guiding principles for parenting in the electronic age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 笔者参加这次会议，希望能找到一些电子时代育儿的指导原则。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. American parents are becoming more doubtful about the benefits technology is said to bring to their children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 美国父母对据称技术给孩子带来的好处越来越怀疑。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Some experts believe that human intelligence develops by the use of hands.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 一些专家认为，人类智力是通过使用双手而发展的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. The author found a former Montessori teacher exercising strict control over her kids, screen time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 作者发现一位前蒙特梭利老师对她的孩子的屏幕时间进行严格控制。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Research shows interaction with people is key to babies, brain development.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 研究表明，与人的互动是婴儿大脑发育的关键。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. So far there has been no scientific proof of the educational benefits of iPads.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When young women were found to make only 82 percent of what their male peers do just one year out of college, many were at a loss to explain it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当发现年轻女性在大学毕业一年后的收入仅为男性同龄人的 82% 时，许多人无法解释这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: All the traditional reasons put forward to interpret the pay gap—that women fall behind when they leave the workforce to raise kids, for example, or that they don’t seek as many management roles— failed to justify this one. These young women didn’t have kids yet. And because they were just one year removed from their undergraduate degrees, few of these women yet had the chance to go after (much less decline) leadership roles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 解释薪酬差距的所有传统原因——例如，女性离开工作岗位去抚养孩子，或者她们不寻求那么多的管理职位——都无法证明这一点的合理性。这些年轻女性还没有孩子。而且由于她们的本科学位仅剩一年，这些女性中很少有人有机会追求（更不用说拒绝）领导角色。

paragraphs.sourceText: But there are other reasons why the pay gap remains so persistent. The first is that no matter how many women may be getting college degrees, the university experience is still an unequal one. The second is that our higher education system is not designed to focus on the economic consequences of our students, years on campus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但薪酬差距如此持续存在还有其他原因。首先，无论有多少女性获得大学学位，大学经历仍然是不平等的。第二，我们的高等教育体系并不是为了关注学生在校期间的经济后果而设计的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now that women are the majority of college students and surpass men in both the number of undergraduate and advanced degrees awarded, one might think the college campus is a pretty equal place. It is not. Studies show that while girls do better than boys in high school, they start to trail off during their college years. They enroll in different kinds of classes, tend to major in less rigorous (非常严格的)subjects, and generally head off with less ambitious plants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 既然女性在大学生中占大多数，并且在获得本科和高级学位的数量上都超过了男性，人们可能会认为大学校园是一个相当平等的地方。它不是。研究表明，虽然女孩在高中时的表现比男孩好，但她们在大学期间开始表现不佳。他们报名参加不同类型的课程，倾向于主修不太严格（非常严格的）科目，并且通常会选择不太雄心勃勃的植物。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, it’s not surprising that even the best educated young women enter the workplace with a slight disadvantage. Their college experience leaves them somewhat confused, still stumbling ( 栽倒) over the dilemmas their grandmothers, generation sought to destroy. Are they supposed to be pretty or smart? Strong or sexy(性感的)？All their lives, today’s young women have been pushed to embrace both perfection and passion—to pursue science and sports, math and theater—and do it all as well as they possibly can. No wonder they are not negotiating for higher salaries as soon as they get out of school. They are too exhausted, and too scared of failing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，即使是受过最好教育的年轻女性在进入职场时也处于轻微劣势也就不足为奇了。他们的大学经历让他们有些困惑，仍然在他们的祖母这一代人试图摧毁的困境中跌跌撞撞。他们应该漂亮还是聪明？坚强还是性感？今天的年轻女性一生都被迫拥抱完美和激情——追求科学和体育、数学和戏剧——并尽其所能地做好这一切。难怪他们一毕业就不会谈判更高的工资。他们太累了，太害怕失败。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Reading leadership literature, you’d sometimes think that everyone has the potential to be an effective leader.
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读领导力文献时，您有时会认为每个人都有潜力成为有效的领导者。

paragraphs.sourceText: I don’t believe that to be true. In fact, I see way fewer truly effective leaders than I see people stuck in positions of leadership who are sadly incompetent and seriously misguided about their own abilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我不相信这是真的。事实上，我看到的真正有效的领导者比我看到的那些被困在领导岗位上的人要少得多，他们可悲的是无能并且对自己的能力严重误导。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of the reason this happens is a lack of honest self-assessment by those who aspire to（追求）leadership in the first place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 发生这种情况的部分原因是那些一开始就渴望（追求）领导力的人缺乏诚实的自我评估。

paragraphs.sourceText: We’ve all met the type of individual who simply must take charge. Whether it’s a decision-making session, a basketball game, or a family outing, they can’t help grabbing the lead dog position and clinging on to it for dear life. They believe they’ve natural born leaders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们都遇到过那种必须负责的人。无论是决策会议、篮球比赛还是家庭郊游，他们都会情不自禁地抢占领头羊的位置，并死死抓住它。他们相信自己是天生的领导者。

paragraphs.sourceText: Truth is, they’re nothing of the sort. True leaders don^ assume that ifs their divine (神圣的) right to take charge every time two or more people get together. Quite the opposite. A great leader will assess each situation on its merits, and will only take charge when their position, the situation, and/or the needs of the moment demand it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实是，它们根本不是这样的。真正的领导者不会认为，每当两个或更多人聚集在一起时，他们就有神圣的权力来负责。恰恰相反。伟大的领导者会根据每种情况的优点进行评估，并且只有在他们的职位、情况和/或当前的需要需要时才会负责。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many business executives confuse leadership with action. They believe that constant motion somehow generates leadership as a byproduct. Faced with any situation that can’t be solved by the sheer force of activity, they generate a dust cloud of impatience. Their one leadership tool is volume: if they think you aren’t working as hard as they think you should, their demands become increasingly louder and harsher.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多企业高管将领导力与行动混为一谈。他们认为，持续的行动在某种程度上会产生领导力作为副产品。面对任何仅靠行动力无法解决的情况，他们都会产生不耐烦的情绪。他们唯一的领导工具就是数量：如果他们认为你没有像他们认为的那样努力工作，他们的要求就会变得越来越响亮、越来越严厉。

paragraphs.sourceText: True leaders understand the value of action, of course, but it isn’t their only tool. In fact, it isn’t even their primary tool. Great leaders see more than everyone else answers, solutions, patterns, problems, opportunities. They know it’s vitally important to do, but they also know that thinking, understanding, reflection and interpretation are equally important.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，真正的领导者了解行动的价值，但这并不是他们唯一的工具。事实上，它甚至不是他们的主要工具。伟大的领导者比其他人看到更多的答案、解决方案、模式、问题和机会。他们知道这样做至关重要，但他们也知道思考、理解、反思和解释同样重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you’re too concerned with outcomes to the extent that you manipulate and intimidate others to achieve those outcomes, then you aren’t leading at all, you’re dictating. A true leader is someone who develops his or her team so that they can and do hit their targets and achieve their goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你太关心结果，以至于操纵和恐吓他人来实现这些结果，那么你根本就不是在领导，而是在发号施令。真正的领导者是发展他或她的团队的人，以便他们能够并且确实实现他们的目标并实现他们的目标。
